proof.text: Write $G=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$, $G'=\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$, $P=(Y'\xrightarrow{f}Y)$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, and $a=\bar y'\in|P_{\bar y}|$. By [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], $f_*$ is characterized by $f_*(h)\cdot\tau_R(z)=\tau_R(h\cdot z)$ for every finite etale $R/Y$ and $z\in|(R\times_YY')_{\bar y'}|$. For $R=P$, the diagonal $d:Y'\to Y'\times_YY'$ is a section of the second projection, and its value $d(\bar y')$ maps under $\tau_P$ to $a$. Every $h\in G'$ fixes $d(\bar y')$: $d$ is a morphism from the final object of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$, whose fibre has one element, and the components of a natural automorphism commute with its fibre map. Hence $f_*(h)\cdot a=a$, so $\operatorname{im}(f_*)\subseteq U$.

source.place: SGA 1, Expose V, Proposition 6.13, pp. 114-115, inclusion of the induced group in the stabilizer; proof omitted there

proof.text: For the reverse inclusion let $g\in U$. Take any $Q=(Z\xrightarrow{q}Y')$ in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$. The composite $f\circ q:Z\to Y$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2), so it is an object $\widetilde Q$ of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$. The fibre $|Q_{\bar y'}|$ identifies with the subset $T_Q=\{z\in|\widetilde Q_{\bar y}|:q(z)=a\}$: a point over $\bar y'$ is exactly a geometric point of $Z$ over $\bar y$ whose composite with $q$ is the specified point $a$ of $Y'$. Since $q:\widetilde Q\to P$ is a morphism in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, naturality of the $G$-action gives $q(g\cdot z)=g\cdot q(z)=g\cdot a=a$ for $z\in T_Q$; thus $g$ preserves $T_Q$. The same holds for $g^{-1}$ because it also fixes $a$, so the restriction is a bijection of $|Q_{\bar y'}|$.

source.place: SGA 1, Expose V, Proposition 6.13, pp. 114-115: objects over the connected object $S$ and the fibre as inverse image of the marked element; proof omitted there

proof.text: If $u:Q\to Q'$ is a morphism over $Y'$, it is also a morphism $\widetilde Q\to\widetilde Q'$ over $Y$, so $u(g\cdot z)=g\cdot u(z)$; the restrictions of step 2 therefore form a natural automorphism of the fibre functor on $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y')$, with inverse obtained from $g^{-1}$. The compact fundamental-group model is isomorphic to the automorphism group of its fibre functor (toAutMulEquiv), so this natural automorphism is represented by an element $h\in G'$. For any $R\in\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, put $Q=R\times_YY'$; the projection $Q\to R$ is a morphism over $Y$ and restricts on $T_Q$ to the bijection $\tau_R$ of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Therefore $\tau_R(h\cdot z)=g\cdot\tau_R(z)$ for every $z\in|Q_{\bar y'}|$. The defining characterization of $f_*$ in that lemma, and faithfulness of evaluation in [def-galois-fibre-functor], imply $f_*(h)=g$. Thus $U\subseteq\operatorname{im}(f_*)$.

title: The image of the induced fundamental-group map is the marked-point stabilizer.
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite etale morphism of connected schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point. Set $t=f\circ s$, let $P=(X\xrightarrow{f}Y)$ be its finite etale cover [def-galois-categories], and let $a=s\in F_t(P)$ for the geometric fibre functor [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $G_X,G_Y$ be compact topological fundamental-group models of $F_s,F_t$, with their natural continuous fibre actions, and put $U=\operatorname{Stab}_{G_Y}(a)$. The homomorphism $f_*:G_X\to G_Y$ induced by pullback and its canonical fibre identification [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] has image $U$.

lean.statement:
theorem fundamentalGroupMap_range_eq_stabilizer_range
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X] [ConnectedSpace Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] [Etale f]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X)
    (GX GY : Type u) [Group GX] [TopologicalSpace GX] [IsTopologicalGroup GX]
    [CompactSpace GX] [∀ Q, MulAction GX ((fiber s).obj Q)]
    [IsFundamentalGroup (fiber s) GX]
    [Group GY] [TopologicalSpace GY] [IsTopologicalGroup GY] [CompactSpace GY]
    [∀ P, MulAction GY ((fiber (s ≫ f)).obj P)]
    [IsFundamentalGroup (fiber (s ≫ f)) GY] :
    let P : Y.FiniteEtale := ⟨Etale.mk f, inferInstanceAs (IsFinite f)⟩
    let a : (fiber (s ≫ f)).obj P := fiberMk (s ≫ f) P s rfl
    let U := MulAction.stabilizer GY a
    (fundamentalGroupMap (pullbackFiberIso f s) GX GY).range = U
